label: Delimiter step after h/k/r/d/e/b/w/q-rich prefix, plus copy-phase re-input of q
explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 62% of activation mass falls at the <DEL> step, but only 7.4% of delimiter steps cross threshold. Whether the <DEL> step fires depends additively on which tokens are in the prefix. h is the strongest contributor (h at prev/prev2 gives 4-5x lift), then k, r, d, e and b, plus a first token of w or q. Requiring >= 3 such tokens before <DEL> roughly triples precision over phase==1 alone. The second component is the copy phase when the re-fed input is q (in_tok q has 6.4x lift, 20% of mass), mostly at recall_idx 1, i.e. sequences that start with q. Smaller, weaker activations occur in the original phase late in long sequences (to_go is large, t 4-9) and on digit 1. It never fires at t=0 and almost never on other copy-phase inputs. The largest activations (up to 0.28) are at <DEL> or at the q right after it in sequences containing h/k. Precision stays low (~0.17) because the token dependence is graded and distributed rather than a clean rule.
